context: The DEFINE default: 0.37.0's own specs are finalised by the released 0.36.1 Finalise with --ci-run, as FBS-231 was, and the new model applies from the first spec after 0.37.0 ships. Three facts read at 639f07bb bear on it: the 0.36.1 Finalise exits 3 on any tree that fails validation (src/cli/finalise.js:228-236), and with rcf-schemas 0.9.0 a criterion carrying verification fails validation; the 0.36.1 Finalise reads Hand: and Hand-Id: trailers for report provenance (src/finalise/ingest.js:447-465); CI's separation job runs the PR head's own audit, so once the stage-prefix slice lands on main the new audit judges every later 0.37.0 pull request.
decision: FBS-228 is built first (stage-keeper ruling 6, under WA-08) and finalised by the released 0.36.1 Finalise in the 0.36.1 flow, with Hand: trailers and no hygiene tests (the 0.36.1 audit classes every test file as test-author); FBS-229 waits until 0.37.0 ships. Before the first Finalise the stage-keeper confirms npm view rcf-lite@0.36.1 version, and publishes 0.36.1 by the deploy path first if it is absent. The schema slice is finalised by the released 0.36.1 Finalise in the 0.36.1 flow (a Test-stage report from the head's rcf verify run --package . --fbs <id> --hand verifier, then the released bin's rcf build mark complete and rcf build finalise --ci-run). The stage-keeper then cuts 0.36.2 from main after the schema slice merges, through the normal release PR, carrying FBS-228 and the schema slice and no other 0.37.0 slice, so every later 0.37.0 spec is finalised by the released 0.36.2 Finalise in the same flow, which accepts the field once the flag slice moves the 0.37.0 criteria onto it. The flag slice is the slice whose own change breaks the 0.36.1 Finalise; without 0.36.2 every spec after it would be refused. From the stage-prefix slice on, every 0.37.0 commit carries its stage prefix and an agreeing Hand: trailer (the 0.36.x Finalise still reads Hand: builder and Hand-Id:); the 0.36.x flow maps onto the new classes: the verifier's report commit is TEST:, the marks are FINALISE:, and the post-mark regeneration of the queue goldens and the phase 3 to 6 view baseline is FINALISE: with Generated-By:, declared in this repository's rcf/separation.json in the stage-prefix slice's round, and the coverage goldens join them in the flag slice's round. From the rounds slice's own round on, the reviewer and the verifier record verdicts with the checkout's own node bin/rcf.js build verdict review and build verdict test (packages/rcf-lite at the branch head), because CI's separation job runs the head's own audit; the verifier's TEST: commit adds the Test-stage report and test.json together, and a failed run records TEST FAIL, which closes the round. WORKAROUND WA-17: no released bin has rcf build verdict before 0.37.0; root-cause item the self-hosting bootstrap of this ADR; review-by the 0.37.0 release. The verifier runs the Test-stage report with RCF_CHECKOUT set to the checkout's absolute path, and testOnly tests read repository files (.github/, git history, scripts/, docs, the root README) through it. The readiness slice is marked complete with rcf build mark FBS-240 complete --no-code-nodes (a genuinely no-code spec). Part B's tests reach main as node:test todo cases in files holding one slice's criteria each (the exception: FBS-228's AC-19401-12 test stays in FBS-227's file test/verify/probe-assertion-0-9-0.test.js, because one file per slice applies only to new files); each slice's round DEFINE, the first DEFINE: commit on its branch, removes its own todo markers. The audit reads the trailer (agreement only) through 0.37.x and ignores it from 0.38.0. The new Finalise (complete) and release Verify (verified) apply from the first spec after 0.37.0 ships; 0.37.0's own specs end at verified in the 0.36.x shape. A spec's regime is the released bin at its Finalise: a round finalised after 0.37.0 ships ends at complete and waits for a release Verify.
consequences: One extra patch release (0.36.2) before the flag slice merges. The Test-stage report mode of rcf verify run (--hand verifier) must keep working through the train, which the Verify slice keeps unchanged. WA-08 (explicit-id bundling) covers the 0.37.0 Builds, and after the backstop slice lands each such bundle also needs a green base-suite record.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the flags as tags until after the release
alternativesConsidered.summary: Move them onto the field in the first round after 0.37.0.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: The flag slice's validate rule would then refuse every later 0.37.0 pull request that adds or amends a criterion without the field, and the WORKAROUND would outlive its review-by.

alternativesConsidered.name: Finalise later 0.37.0 specs with the head's own Finalise
alternativesConsidered.summary: Use the new Finalise as it lands.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A spec would be finalised by the code it ships, and the new Finalise needs verdict records and test strength that earlier slices of the same train had not shipped yet.

alternativesConsidered.name: Order the flag slice last
alternativesConsidered.summary: Delay the field until every other slice is finalised.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Verify, Finalise and coverage depend on the field to tell external from testOnly.

title: Self-hosting 0.37.0: its own specs are finalised by the released 0.36.x Finalise, the pin move ships first as 0.36.2, and the separation audit accepts an agreeing trailer through 0.37.x
